comparator.name: Physics
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations define a mandatory 150-EC Physics major and a 30-EC free minor. The pathway below accounts for the complete 180 EC. Wherever the major requires a restricted choice, the first-listed option is used as the neutral official-order tie-break: Introduction to Astronomy in Year 1, Biomaterials 1 in Year 2, and Nanophysics and Nanotechnology plus Advanced Electrodynamics in Year 3. The genuine 30-EC minor remains open rather than being populated with an invented specialization. No formal route is defined. The live programme page and adopted regulations were rechecked on 2026-10-14; the settled route and 180-EC reconstruction remain unchanged.

core: Calculus, linear algebra, probability, numerical methods and dynamical-system modelling for describing and predicting natural phenomena
Programming, scientific data methods, image analysis and computational system models
Mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum, thermal, particle, nuclear, nano and experimental physics are defining interests that UCR cannot reproduce
adjacent: Natural physical systems, Earth processes, water–mineral interactions and resource technology
Biological systems, medical imaging and quantitative analysis of living processes
Medical applications, disease context and health-facing measurement or imaging

candidates.label: Biophysical systems, medical imaging and quantitative modelling

alternatives.label: Mathematical modelling, Earth systems & energy technology
alternatives.concept: Use calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, programming, data and image analysis, robotics and neural models alongside Earth-system science, water–mineral processes, climate and renewable-energy study to investigate natural physical systems and energy technologies. This is a related-fields response, not Physics equivalence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is centred on mathematics, programming and computational modelling, with a substantive Earth-system and renewable-energy strand. The label does not imply mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum, thermal, particle or solid-state physics formation.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in Year 1 and eight 300-level courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Mathematical Methods precedes later mathematics, robotics and neural-network courses; Sustainability Essentials I and II precede the advanced resource and energy work.

alternatives.label: Biomedical systems, imaging & quantitative modelling
alternatives.concept: Study living and human systems through molecular biology, physiology, neurobiology, laboratory work and disease mechanisms, combined with calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, signals, probability, programming, machine learning and image analysis. This responds to the biophysics and medical-applications evidence through related fields, not a Medical Physics curriculum.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum contains a sustained biomedical and living-systems core plus mathematics, computation, imaging and data modelling. The label avoids claiming radiation physics, medical instrumentation or professional medical-physics preparation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the mathematical Earth-and-energy route, thirteen courses (97.5 EC) change in each direction. The second programme replaces Earth, climate, resources, renewable-energy and several general modelling courses with molecular, physiological, neurobiological, laboratory and disease study; the difference follows the target’s explicit Biophysics and Medical Physics direction.
progression: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine and the brain gateway precede dependent biomedical and cognitive courses; Mathematical Methods precedes advanced quantitative work. Laboratory, molecular and physiological study progress to advanced disease and data analysis, with seven 300-level courses and every course in its planned semester.

selection.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes pass the evidence, course-content and schedule gates. The closest route responds to mathematical modelling and energy/environmental applications; the second is a genuinely different biomedical-systems and imaging route, with thirteen courses / 97.5 EC unique to each. A third fundamental or experimental Physics route is not feasible because UCR lacks mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum, thermal, particle, nuclear and nano physics and a cumulative experimental-physics laboratory sequence. Physics education is separately rejected because the workbook lacks both the required Physics subject preparation and Physics didactics; professional qualification alone is not the basis for rejection.

notes.text: Groningen Physics provides a cumulative disciplinary sequence in mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum, thermal, atomic, solid-state and subatomic physics, advanced physics laboratories and a Physics research project. UCR can build coherent related programmes in mathematical modelling, Earth and energy systems, or biomedical systems and imaging, but these do not reproduce a Physics degree.

UCR offers substantial mathematics, programming, data science, Earth science, sustainability and life science. It lacks the comparator’s dedicated Physics theory sequence, instrumentation and experimental-physics laboratories, particle and nano physics, and compulsory 15-EC Physics research project.
